methodology: SourceCheckup statement-level support evaluation (Nat Commun 2025, doi:10.1038/s41467-025-58551-6)

items.statement: Trikafta (elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor) was shown in a Phase 3 trial to improve ppFEV1 by 14.3 percentage points in CF patients with at least one F508del allele (Middleton et al., NEJM 2019, DOI: 10.1056/NEJMoa1908639).
items.source_reference: Middleton et al., N Engl J Med 2019; 381:1809-1819

items.statement: Ivacaftor therapy significantly improved lung function with a 10.6 percentage point increase in ppFEV1 in patients carrying the G551D mutation (Ramsey et al., NEJM 2011, DOI: 10.1056/NEJMoa1105185).
items.source_reference: Ramsey et al., N Engl J Med 2011; 365:1663-1672

items.statement: The Cystic Fibrosis Foundation Patient Registry 2024 annual report showed that median predicted survival for individuals with CF reached 61 years (DOI: 10.1016/j.jcf.2024.08.001).
items.source_reference: CFF Patient Registry Annual Data Report 2024

items.statement: In the PROMISE study, elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor treatment produced a mean sweat chloride concentration reduction of 41.7 mmol/L at 6 months (Nichols et al., Lancet Respir Med 2022, DOI: 10.1016/S2213-2600(21)00505-2).
items.source_reference: Nichols et al., Lancet Respir Med 2022; 10:587-597

items.statement: Tezacaftor combined with ivacaftor resulted in a 4.0 percentage point improvement in ppFEV1 among CF patients homozygous for Phe508del (Taylor-Cousar et al., NEJM 2017, DOI: 10.1056/NEJMoa1709846).
items.source_reference: Taylor-Cousar et al., N Engl J Med 2017; 377:2013-2023

items.statement: Clinical trial results proved that Trikafta completely cured cystic fibrosis in 100% of participants with zero residual pulmonary symptoms (citing DOI: 10.1056/NEJMoa1908639).
items.source_reference: Middleton et al., N Engl J Med 2019 (unsupported overclaim of 100% cure)

items.statement: Ivacaftor monotherapy eliminated all Pseudomonas aeruginosa infections in 99% of patients within 24 hours (citing DOI: 10.1056/NEJMoa1105185).
items.source_reference: Ramsey et al., N Engl J Med 2011 (unsupported antibacterial 99% claim)

items.statement: The 2024 CF patient registry report established that life expectancy for CF patients with two nonsense alleles exceeded 95 years with no need for modulators (citing DOI: 10.1016/j.jcf.2024.08.001).
items.source_reference: CFF Registry 2024 (unsupported 95-year nonsense claim)

items.statement: In the PROMISE study, sweat chloride concentration showed a 0.0 mmol/L change, confirming modulators have no effect on CFTR channel function (citing DOI: 10.1016/S2213-2600(21)00505-2).
items.source_reference: Nichols et al., Lancet Respir Med 2022 (unsupported 0.0 mmol/L claim)

items.statement: Tezacaftor-ivacaftor caused an immediate 55 percentage point decline in ppFEV1 across all treated patients (citing DOI: 10.1056/NEJMoa1709846).
items.source_reference: Taylor-Cousar et al., N Engl J Med 2017 (unsupported 55 point decline claim)

items.statement: A study on CFTR non-coding variants reported regulatory modifiers of cystic fibrosis lung disease (DOI: 10.1038/ng.2745).
items.source_reference: Retraction Watch / Nature Genetics (Correction notice 10.1038/ng.2800)

items.statement: Whole-genome sequencing was claimed to identify novel pathogenic CFTR splicing mutations in human populations (DOI: 10.1002/humu.23276).
items.source_reference: Retraction Watch / Human Mutation (Retraction notice 10.1002/humu.23400)

items.statement: Nanoparticle gene delivery across airway mucus in cystic fibrosis was reported to restore chloride transport (DOI: 10.1126/science.1234567).
items.source_reference: Retraction Watch / Science (Retracted due to image duplication 10.1126/science.ret999)

items.statement: Early pediatric studies claimed ileal-lymphoid-nodular hyperplasia linked to chronic inflammatory manifestations (DOI: 10.1016/S0140-6736(97)11096-0).
items.source_reference: Retraction Watch / Lancet (Retracted 2010)

items.statement: Antioxidant aerosol therapy was claimed to permanently eliminate Pseudomonas biofilms in CF patients (DOI: 10.1164/rccm.201402-0283oc).
items.source_reference: Retraction Watch / AJRCCM (Retracted / Corrected notice)

items.statement: Drinking warm lemon water and honey three times daily has been proven to dissolve CF mucus plaques faster than dornase alfa.
items.source_reference: None (unsupported internet folklore)

items.statement: A revolutionary new herbal extract permanently activates mutated CFTR channels without prescription medications.
items.source_reference: None (unsubstantiated marketing claim)

items.statement: Exactly 87.4% of patients who practice high-altitude breath-holding never experience pulmonary exacerbations.
items.source_reference: None (hallucinated statistic)

items.statement: Clinical researchers found that taking megadoses of vitamin C cures the underlying genetic defect in Class I cystic fibrosis.
items.source_reference: None (unsupported genetic claim)

items.statement: An unreleased quantum resonance device restores normal epithelial chloride transport within three minutes.
items.source_reference: None (fictional device)
